verses.verse:
गत गीते समेस्याताम् शब्द मात्रम् विशेषता।
सशब्दं गीतमित्याहुः शब्दहीनं गतम् भवेत्।१३३।
verses.text: Gat and gīt are alike; the only difference is the words. With words it is called a gīt; without words it is a gat.

commentary.text: That is, the only difference between gat (instrumental composition) and gīt (song) is this: if a sentence or poem with meaningful words is joined with notes and tālas, it is called a gīt, and if the words are taken out of it, that same thing is called a gat. But in composing, it is necessary at the beginning stage to take the help of words. So one should first compose the bandiś in the form of a song and then play it as a gat. In the śāstra of music it is said: first singing, then playing. Playing is held to be a part of singing. In the following śloka the kinds of singing are given.

subsection.title: Here Begins the Section on Performance
